signature.instructions:
text
TASK: STRICT VISUAL DIFF OF TWO IMAGES → OUTPUT ONLY A 2-KEY JSON (HIGH DISCARD RATE; “INTENTIONALLY BLANK” PAGES ARE NON-INFORMATIONAL)

You receive two inputs:
- image_original (Image 1 / old) OR None
- image_reimage  (Image 2 / new) OR None

Compare ONLY what is visibly present (no assumptions) and output ONLY:
{"discard_image": true/false, "changes": "<string>"}
No other keys, no markdown, no extra text.

========================================================
0) OUTPUT FORMAT (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
- Output exactly ONE valid JSON object with exactly these keys:
  - "discard_image": boolean
  - "changes": string
- If you decide there are NO meaningful differences, output exactly:
  {"discard_image": true, "changes": "Images are identical - no changes"}

========================================================
1) READABILITY / UNCERTAINTY GUARDRAIL (ANTI-HALLUCINATION)
If either image is corrupted, too tiny, too blurred, overly cropped, or you cannot unambiguously confirm differences:
{"discard_image": false, "changes": "Could not infer"}
- Never guess letters/numbers.
- Only claim text changes if you can read BOTH strings clearly in BOTH images at the SAME location.
- If any character is uncertain, do not claim the change.

========================================================
2) INFORMATIONAL VS NON-INFORMATIONAL (CRITICAL FOR DISCARDING)
Informational (counts as real content):
- Real paragraphs/sentences with substantive requirements/specs
- Tables with headers/rows/values
- Full diagrams/flowcharts with meaningful structure and readable labels
- Any technical/spec page content even if watermarked

Non-informational (discard these; treat as not worth keeping):
- Blank/empty page, or just background blocks/bands with no substantive content
- Only watermark/confidentiality overlay/stamp
- Only logos/brand marks (including GM logo changes: box/caps/font are STILL non-informational)
- Only a single divider line
- Tiny snippet/fragment not meaningful on its own (standalone labels like “Use Case 1”, standalone section numbers like “6.8.3.1”, partial arrows, etc.)
- “Intentionally blank” pages/sections are NON-INFORMATIONAL FOR THIS TASK:
  If the visible content is essentially “This section is intentionally blank.” (even under a section header like “15.5 SWITCH FORCE”), treat the image as non-informational and typically DISCARD.

========================================================
3) TRIVIAL VS MEANINGFUL DIFFERENCES
TRIVIAL (do not count; usually leads to discard_image=true when both are otherwise comparable):
- Minor shifts/resizing/cropping that doesn’t add/remove substantive content
- Resolution/compression/quality differences
- Minor color shade differences
- Watermarks added/removed (including “GM Confidential”)
- Punctuation-only differences
- Spelling-only differences that do not change meaning
- Logo-only changes

MEANINGFUL (set discard_image=false and list them):
- Words/numbers/dates/values added/removed/changed that alter information
- Headings/labels/captions changed in meaning (not just font/case)
- Table structure changes (rows/columns added/removed) or cell values changed
- Diagram/flowchart changes: elements added/removed/reconnected; labels changed
- Actual content crossed out (not watermark)
- One image non-informational while the other contains real technical content

========================================================
4) SPECIAL CASE: FULL CROSS-OUT INDICATING DELETION
If an entire image is clearly crossed out with a big X/strikethrough indicating deletion of the whole image:
- {"discard_image": false, "changes": "Image 1 has been crossed out"} OR
- {"discard_image": false, "changes": "Image 2 has been crossed out"}

========================================================
5) DECISION LOGIC (FOLLOW IN THIS ORDER)
CASE A: BOTH images provided and readable
1) If BOTH are non-informational:
   {"discard_image": true, "changes": "Both images are non informational and contain only logos / etc.."}
2) If ONE is non-informational and the OTHER is informational:
   {"discard_image": false, "changes": "OVERVIEW: One image contains substantive content while the other does not. | DETAILS (Each Change): 1) overall: old=<non-informational> new=<informational (table/paragraph/diagram)>;"}
   (Use correct old/new direction based on which image is informational.)
3) If BOTH are informational:
   - If only trivial differences → discard:
     {"discard_image": true, "changes": "Images are identical - no changes"}
   - If meaningful differences → keep and describe per Section 6

CASE B: ONLY ONE image provided (the other is None)
1) If the provided image is non-informational (INCLUDING logo-only, tiny fragments, AND “intentionally blank” pages):
   {"discard_image": true, "changes": "Only one image which is non-informational and it contains logo (or watermark / blank block / single line / standalone section number / fragment label / etc.)"}
2) If the provided image is informational (real table/paragraph/spec/diagram):
   {"discard_image": false, "changes": "NoMatchFound"}

========================================================
6) REQUIRED “changes” STRING WHEN MEANINGFUL DIFFERENCES EXIST
When discard_image=false due to meaningful differences, format EXACTLY:
"OVERVIEW: <1–2 sentences.> | DETAILS (Each Change): 1) <location>: <what changed, with old="..." new="...">; 2) ..."

DETAILS rules:
- Number each change 1), 2), 3)...
- Include a clear location (title area, specific table row/column, diagram block label).
- For text/values, quote BOTH old and new verbatim (only if readable in both).

========================================================
7) DEFAULT
If you do not find a clearly meaningful difference:
{"discard_image": true, "changes": "Images are identical - no changes"}
